parameters.jsCode:
const response = $input.item.json || {};
const parsedSearch = $('Parse Search Query').first().json;
const records = Array.isArray(response.records) ? response.records : [];

const selectedRecords = records
  .filter((record) => record && record.url)
  .slice(0, 5)
  .map((record, index) => ({
    sourceNumber: index + 1,
    rank: record.rank ?? index + 1,
    title: record.title || '',
    url: record.url,
    description: record.description || '',
    content: String(record.content || record.reader?.content || '').slice(0, 5000)
  }));

const searchContext = selectedRecords.length
  ? selectedRecords.map((record) => [
      `SOURCE ${record.sourceNumber}`,
      `Title: ${record.title}`,
      `URL: ${record.url}`,
      `Description: ${record.description}`,
      'Content:',
      record.content || '(No page content returned. Use title/description only if needed.)'
    ].join('\n')).join('\n\n---\n\n')
  : '(No search records were returned.)';

const finalAnswerPrompt = [
  'You answer user questions using only the provided web search sources.',
  '',
  'Rules:',
  '- Answer the original question directly.',
  '- Use the provided sources only.',
  '- If sources disagree, say so briefly.',
  '- Be practical and concise.',
  '- Include timing guidance clearly.',
  '- Explain whether the timer starts before or after boiling.',
  '- Do not invent sources.',
  '- Return valid JSON only.',
  '',
  'Original user question:',
  parsedSearch.userQuery,
  '',
  'Search query used:',
  parsedSearch.searchQuery,
  '',
  'Web search sources:',
  searchContext,
  '',
  'Return this exact JSON shape:',
  JSON.stringify({
    answer: 'string',
    sourceNumbersUsed: [1, 2],
    confidence: 'high | medium | low'
  }, null, 2)
].join('\n');

return {
  json: {
    userQuery: parsedSearch.userQuery,
    searchQuery: parsedSearch.searchQuery,
    searchStatus: response.status || 'unknown',
    recordCount: response.recordCount ?? records.length,
    sourceCount: selectedRecords.length,
    sources: selectedRecords.map(({ sourceNumber, rank, title, url }) => ({ sourceNumber, rank, title, url })),
    searchContext,
    finalAnswerPrompt,
    rawSearchResponsePreview: {
      status: response.status,
      provider: response.provider,
      candidateCount: response.candidateCount,
      recordCount: response.recordCount,
      metadata: response.metadata
    }
  }
};

parameters.content:
## POC step 1 — HTTP OpenRouter version
Hardcoded user query → OpenRouter HTTP inference formats Brave query → existing Brave+Jina callable workflow → OpenRouter HTTP inference generates final answer.

This version avoids the OpenRouter Chat Model node/model dropdown.

## OpenRouter credential
Create an **HTTP Header Auth** credential, not an OpenRouter account credential.

Name: `Authorization`
Value: `Bearer <your OpenRouter API key>`

Then reselect it in both OpenRouter HTTP Request nodes.

## After import
1. Reselect the OpenRouter HTTP Header Auth credential on both OpenRouter HTTP nodes.
2. Open **Call Web Search Workflow** and select your local **Web Search - Brave API + Jina Reader Workflow**.
3. Make sure that workflow has Brave configured and its Jina Reader sub-workflow selected.
